title: Tortilla Chips 300g

drivers.name: Price increase (3.97 vs 3.83)
drivers.evidence: Two consecutive weeks at $3.97 saw sales drop to 106 and 75 units (vs baseline 124.2), a 15–40% decline. Noise-adjusted effect shrunk toward 1.0, but persistent trend suggests ~12% reduction.

drivers.name: Store closure (Mon)
drivers.evidence: One day closed in a 7-day week reduces sales by ~14%. No past closure data, but store-level impact is direct and measurable.

adjustment.analysis: The target week has no events but a price increase to $3.97 (+3.7%) and a store closure on Monday. The baseline trend shows a -10.5% decline over 13 weeks, but recent weeks (post-2026-09-28) show low sales (75–108 units), suggesting price sensitivity. The price increase is not a promotion, so it likely reduces demand. The store closure removes one day of sales, reducing volume by ~14%. The historical price effect is not directly observed, but the 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-05 drops at $3.97 suggest a negative response. No past promotion at this price or overlap with closures. The uplift model suggests no change, but judgment overrides this due to known price and closure drivers.

PRODUCT: Tortilla Chips 300g | category Snacks | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-22 (6 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 3.97 (+3.7% vs regular price 3.83)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 124.2 | 5%-95%: 77.4 - 200.4 | 10%-90%: 88.8 - 170.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-29% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
